name: C3is Inc.

profile.description: C3is Inc. is an Athens-based owner of drybulk carriers and tankers (Handysize bulkers, an Aframax tanker and recently acquired MR product tankers) carrying iron ore, grain, crude and refined products. It was spun off from Imperial Petroleum in June 2023 and is linked to the shipping interests of Haris Vafeias. H1 2026 revenue rose to $35.6M from $19.4M with net income of $13.2M as daily TCE rates more than doubled, but the share price has collapsed to about $0.50 after repeated reverse splits (1:100 and 1:2.5 in 2024, 1:20 in January 2026 and 1:7 in April 2026) and warrant-heavy equity raises, leaving a market cap of under $2M.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): C3is has expanded from a drybulk spin-off into tankers, buying two product tankers for $39.8M with the second delivered August 6, 2026, which lifted Q2 voyage revenue 124% to $24.0M [2][3]. This is fleet growth in a commodity market rather than product innovation. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI strategy or deployment was found. Market Share (0/2): With a handful of vessels C3is is a price-taker in global drybulk and tanker markets. Pipeline (0/2): No newbuild program or announced vessel pipeline beyond the completed acquisitions was found. R&D (0/1): FY2025 R&D spending was zero [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): C3is describes itself only in generic terms as a provider of international seaborne transportation services, with no articulated purpose beyond operating vessels [1]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs were found. Employee Retention (0/2): No employee or retention data is disclosed; the company has no reported headcount. Insider Buying (0/2): No open-market insider purchases were found; instead, equity has been issued through unit offerings with resettable Class D warrants carrying a floor price of $0.428, a structure that transfers value away from common holders [5][6].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR TRIGGERED: avg daily volume of 1.30M shares at $0.50 equals about $650K per day, below the $1,000,000 threshold, so Infrastructure is 0 regardless of other metrics (recent daily volume of 253K shares is even thinner) [7]. For reference, the underlying metrics would otherwise score well: D/E of 0.06% (no bank debt), ROE of 22.3%, TTM profit margin of 41.3%, revenue growth of 123.9% YoY and a FY2021-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 53.4% (derived from FMP annual statements, $6.27M to $34.76M over four years) [4][7]. Forward P/E and PEG are unavailable because no analyst estimates exist.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): C3is moves physical cargo (iron ore, grain, crude and refined products) on ocean-going vessels, a business AI cannot substitute; earnings are driven by charter rates, with daily TCE rising from $16,466 to $40,260 in Q2 2026 on market conditions, not technology [2][3]. Optimization software may compress voyage inefficiencies industry-wide, but that does not threaten vessel ownership. AI Opportunity (0/1): The company generates no AI-related revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens C3is is a finite player: it has no articulated cause, and its capital-markets behavior (four reverse splits in about two years and resettable warrant financings) optimizes for keeping a listing and raising cash rather than building something that endures. Its only infinite-game credit is a modest shift from drybulk into tankers.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): C3is exists to own and charter vessels; no purpose statement beyond 'seaborne transportation services' was found, and nothing suggests a vision of a better future that would inspire sacrifice [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The company discloses no headcount or culture information, and no evidence of an empowered internal team was found. A thinly staffed vessel-holding structure tied to a sponsor family offers no basis for Sinek's Circle of Safety.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): As a small price-taker, C3is shows no competitive self-reflection; management commentary focuses on charter rates and fleet utilization (78.6% in Q2 2026) rather than learning from peers [3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): C3is has shifted its fleet mix from drybulk toward tankers, adding an Aframax and two MR product tankers, which more than doubled revenue as tanker rates rose [2][3]. This is opportunistic rate-chasing within shipping rather than a cause-driven reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Leadership has repeatedly chosen dilutive financing with resettable warrants and reverse splits (1:100, 1:2.5, 1:20, 1:7) to preserve the Nasdaq listing, decisions that protect the corporate vehicle at shareholders' expense rather than sacrificing short-term results for long-term capability [2][5][6].

investment_thesis: The bull case is purely operational: charter rates have surged, with Q2 2026 daily TCE of $40,260 (+145% YoY), H1 2026 revenue of $35.6M versus $19.4M and H1 net income of $13.2M, and the company has no bank debt after funding two product tankers ($39.8M) [2][3]. On paper, a TTM profit margin of 41% and ROE of 22% against a market cap under $2M look extraordinarily cheap [7].
thesis_continued: The bear case dominates: the equity has been structurally diluted through units with resettable warrants (Class D floor of $0.428) and four reverse splits since April 2024, so earnings accrue to new warrant holders rather than existing shareholders, and the stock trades at $0.50 versus a 50-day average of $1.15 [5][6][7]. Daily dollar volume of about $650K fails IOWN's liquidity floor, utilization was only 78.6% in Q2 due to an idle spot Aframax and dry-docking, and earnings depend entirely on volatile tanker and drybulk rates [3]. A further reverse split or Nasdaq deficiency notice is a real risk at a sub-$1 price.
key_catalysts: Sustained tanker charter strength keeping daily TCE near Q2 2026's $40,260 level, which drove a 124% jump in voyage revenue [3]
Full-quarter contribution from the second acquired product tanker delivered August 6, 2026 [2]
Higher fleet utilization than Q2 2026's 78.6% once dry-docking is complete and the spot Aframax is employed [3]
key_risks: Continued dilution from resettable warrants with a $0.428 floor and further equity raises, which has already required four reverse splits since 2024 [5][6]
Nasdaq minimum bid price deficiency with shares at about $0.50, risking another reverse split or delisting [7]
Reversal in tanker and drybulk charter rates, which would erase the earnings gains driven almost entirely by TCE rates more than doubling [3]
